exposure: Pre-existing kidney disease vs. no pre-existing kidney disease
Immunoglobulin A vasculitis (IgA-V), History of IgA-V, Pre-existing kidney disease
History of IgA-V (cases) vs. IgA-V developed after pregnancy vs. healthy controls
cohort: 26 pregnancies in patients with a history of IgA-V, 15 pregnancies in women who later developed IgA-V, and 52 pregnancies in healthy women
finding: Women with a history of IgA-V are at higher risk for gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia, particularly those with renal involvement, but maternal and newborn outcomes are generally favorable with no vasculitis flares observed during pregnancy.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was performed more often in the group with a history of IgA-V compared to the other groups (27% vs 0% vs 10%, p = 0.04).
